title: Traffic sculpting & safety-holster for variant evolution: capacity-aware shadowing and rollback heuristics
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a single, reusable subsystem to gradually shape production traffic for model variants while accounting for regional capacity tiers and triggering deterministic, explainable auto-rollbacks. Current rollout tooling can do simple weighted canaries or shadowing, but it doesn't consider per-variant resource elasticity (GPU memory/throughput), region-level watermarks, or a unified safety holster that pauses traffic and drains to safe variants when combined signals indicate degradation.

Goal: Build 'Traffic Sculptor' — a policy-driven routing layer that: 1) supports progressive shadowing with adaptive ramp-ups based on realtime capacity signals; 2) evaluates compatibility and semantic regressions via lightweight probes; 3) computes a safety score (latency + error + quality + cost delta + capacity headroom) and triggers staged rollback actions (throttle -> divert -> pause -> rollback) with audit trails; 4) exposes observability and manual override hooks in Console and the rollout API.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full model-level semantic evals (only lightweight probe-based signals) and won't change core admission control for Dedicated pools—those are covered in a follow-on that integrates with autoscaler hooks.
acceptance_criteria: A Traffic Sculptor policy type exists and can be attached to an existing ModelDeployment resource via API
Can perform progressive shadowing: 0% -> 1% -> X% based on a capacity-safe ramp schedule computed from region/gpu tier metrics
Safety score computed from configurable signals (p95 latency, 5xx rate, token-cost-delta, probe-failure-rate, capacity-headroom) and documented formula
Policy supports staged rollback actions: throttle, divert to fallback variant, pause new traffic, and full rollback; rollback reason stored in audit logs
Console shows per-policy dashboard: current ramp, safety score, contributing signals, recent probe samples, and a single-click pause/rollback
End-to-end tests that simulate region saturation cause the policy to divert to fallback variant within SLA-defined window in the test harness
implementation_steps: Design policy schema and protobuf for Traffic Sculptor; include weight schedule, probe config, signal thresholds, and rollback ladder
Add a policy compiler that translates Traffic Sculptor config into runtime routing rules and admission fences
Integrate region & tiered capacity signals from Metrics API (region GPU free slots, queue depth, executor saturation) into safety score engine
Add lightweight semantic probes: synthetic user journey that runs in shadow mode and reports similarity/quality score and probe latency
Implement staged rollback actuator with four actions (throttle -> divert -> pause -> rollback) and persisted audit record in Deployments DB
Expose Console UI widgets and API endpoints for manual override, real-time score, and probe traces
Create integration tests in the deployment simulator that injects load, saturates a region, and validates rollback ladder timing
Ship dogfood rollout to internal feature flag: run on 2 low-traffic model deployments for 2 weeks before wider rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler and safety score formula
Simulated region saturation tests in the deployment simulator (scenario matrix across small/medium/large GPU tiers)
Canary on internal deployments with staged rollout and manual watch windows
A/B run comparing token-cost-delta and latency impact with and without KV-cache priming during shadow ramps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives from semantic probes can cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use conservative thresholds initially and combine probe signal with latency/error/cost metrics before triggering actions.
Risk: Cross-region routing flaps under transient cloud API errors. Mitigation: add hysteresis and require sustained safety score breaches for N consecutive windows before divert/rollback.
Risk: Increased complexity for customers on Dedicated. Mitigation: default to opt-in and provide a 'read-only advisory' mode that only reports suggested actions until explicitly enabled.
Risk: Auditability and compliance. Mitigation: persist all safety score inputs and policy decisions with timestamps and actor (system or user) to Deployments DB for 90d retention.
